Sibling of the parked AddRock3 (Sonnet grinder, 6 attempts, best build/grind/ar54.c, 189 vs 191 bytes, 55/76 opcodes): 5x5 shape table at Dx8+0x870a indexed id*25 + row + col*5, check pass against MapA cells > 0x10 at x*64 + y + col, then the write pass; the table pointer is formed once per row and advanced by 5. The index table is walked recordCount times: each entry's stored offset seeks the original file (+0xe), its 10-byte record header and body are read and rewritten into the temp file at the running offset (WinPrintf progress message per record), the index entry is updated in place to the new offset, and the running offset/counter advance. Finally both files close, the old .dat is unlinked, the pack buffer freed, the temp file renamed over '%s.dat' (the slot's own stored name), reopened, and the slot's file/freeBytes(-=wasted)/wastedBytes(=0)/dirty(=1) updated. Given the size (547 bytes, largest DB target) and single attempt, the remaining register/frame/branch divergence (cfg_shape_match false) needs several more explained revisions before matching; not pursued further given session time. Key uncertain areas: the exact 4 reserved words of the file header (unobserved, zero-initialized here), and whether the per-record loop is a counted while (matching my candidate) or a pointer-limit while (matching the sibling DBRecall/ClearObjToEOL functions' preference for pointer-decrement loops in this same compiler profile).

Every subsequent target/candidate byte difference after 0xb1 is exactly this 3-byte shift plus the already-expected CONST/selector fixup normalization (see reconstruction_rules). Seven explained revisions failed to reproduce this dead store from equivalent C: 'cnt = ++TilesDugB; if (cnt>0)', 'if ((cnt=++TilesDugB)>0)', separate '++TilesDugB; cnt=TilesDugB;', a nested block 'int cnt=++TilesDugB;' at point of use, and a guard-clause 'if (cnt<=0) goto smooth;' all get the store eliminated by the compiler (326-byte candidate, matches 119/135 opcodes). Declaring cnt 'volatile' does force the store (328-byte candidate) but also forces an unwanted reload ('mov ax,[bp-2]' before the compare and again before the second division's cdq) that the target does not have, dropping the match to 115/135. No plain-C phrasing tried reproduces write-without-reload for this value under compiler_profile msc700 /AL /G2 /Gs /Oelw /NTSIMONE_MODULE.

Parameter naming/declaration order cannot affect this: both parameters bind to bp+6/bp+8 purely by call-site push order regardless of C parameter names, so no source-level lever changes which stack slot the compiler homes into SI vs DI in an isolated compile; this only differs from the sibling DigTileThemB by which physical register got chosen, suggesting the true allocation was influenced by the function's real position/neighbors in its historical translation unit (unit simone:16AE), which an isolated single-function compile cannot reproduce. Aside from the SI/DI swap, first_structural_difference at target offset 0xad (173) is the identical dead 'mov word ptr [bp-2],ax' (cnt=++TilesDugR spill) already documented and unresolved on DigTileThemB; see that block's evidence for the exhausted C-phrasing attempts (goto-tail, assignment-in-condition, split statements, nested block, guard-clause inversion, volatile) that could not reproduce it without adding an unwanted reload.
